result.manual:
Optical table: 2400 x 1200 mm breadboard. Coordinates in mm: x along the long side (0..2400), z across (0..1200), height = height above the breadboard (y). Yaw angles are in degrees in the table plane, measured from +x toward +z.
Laser housing (amplifier, 800 nm, ~100 fs FWHM, 1 kHz, pulse energy stability ~3% rms, and an OPA pumped by it) at the x = 2400 end. Inside the housing the amplifier output is split: one part exits at the 800 nm port (355 mm of path from the split), the other goes to the OPA input (373 mm of path from the split).
800 nm output port (arm '800nm'): x=2250, z=294, height=120, beam travelling toward -x (yaw 180). Collimated, 0.5 mm 1/e^2 radius, horizontally polarised.
OPA output port (arm 'opa'; OPA, 1300 nm, ~60 fs FWHM): x=2250, z=935, height=158, beam travelling toward -x (yaw 180). Collimated, 0.80 mm 1/e^2 radius, horizontally polarised.
Laser housings occupy x > 2250 around each port. Both shutters start closed. Any beam leaving the table is a laser-safety violation (logged).
Desk (computer, monitor, scope, stage controller) at x=-300, z=600, beside the x=0 end. You walk on a walkway 300 mm outside the table edge (tool responses give your position as you_at, or 'desk') at 0.5 m/s, and can reach 0.6 m in from the table edge. Catalogue, datasheets, manuals, buying, camera, signal reads, motorised stage moves and scans happen at the desk; knobs, placement, the IR card and the tape measure happen at the table. knob(..., watch=true) also returns a camera frame if you are within 1.5 m of the desk. measure_path is a tape measure along the beam (good to about +/-5 mm).
Placing a part takes ~5 min and lands within ~1 mm of the requested position; yaw set by eye is good to ~0.5 deg.
Already on the table, free: a sample mount with f = 100 mm achromatic lens(es); a flip-in Si CMOS alignment camera at the sample (also images the lens plane), specified 400-1000 nm; a zoomed Si CMOS signal camera looking at the sample (400-1000 nm) through an empty filter holder; a 1 GHz oscilloscope at the desk; an IR/visible viewer card (400-1700 nm); and beam-block shutters at both output ports.

OPA user manual (excerpt). Current output 1300 nm, ~60 fs, horizontally polarised. Signal and idler outputs (1100-2600 nm) leave after the parametric stages; visible outputs (450-700 nm) are generated in the frequency-mixing extension, which adds ~580 mm of internal path. Internal optical path from the OPA pump input to the output port in the current (signal) configuration, factory calibration for this unit: 1527 mm.

Delay stage manual. place(stage, x, z, height, yaw): (x, z) is the stage reference point at the front of the rail and height the retroreflector apex height; yaw is the rail direction, pointing from the reference point toward the retroreflector. The retroreflector apex sits 90 mm + stage position along the rail from the reference point. Hollow gold retroreflector, entrance face 40 mm in front of the apex, clear aperture radius 19.1 mm. Stage positions are in mm from 0 to the travel limit.

Sample mount, 90-degree crossing version. The experiment requires the two beams to cross at a full angle of 90 deg at the sample, each arriving 45 deg from the sample normal through its own lens (both beams through the same lens is not the required geometry). place(sample, x, z, height, yaw): (x, z, height) is the sample point, yaw the direction the sample's front face points (its normal). Two f = 100 mm achromatic lenses, each 100 mm before the sample point on its own axis: lens A axis along (yaw + 135 deg), lens B along (yaw + 225 deg) (directions light travels through them). Lens clear aperture radius 12.7 mm, 2" mount rings (outer radius 25.4 mm). install(part_id) swaps the diagnostic (or the signal-camera filter) without moving the mount. The alignment and signal cameras look at the sample head-on along its normal, from the front. Flip-in alignment camera (Si CMOS, specified 400-1000 nm; CAM-VSWIR replaces it): view_camera('sample') images the sample (5.5 um pixels, field of view +/-4.0 mm); view_camera('lens') images the lens plane. Each spot reports its centroid, 1/e^2 radius and relative_power (fraction of that beam's output power reaching the sample, ~2% reading noise). The camera does not distinguish wavelengths: spots are listed by position. Sample image axes: h horizontal in the sample surface, positive toward (yaw + 90 deg); v up; the sample point is h = v = 0. Lens images report which lens (A or B) and h, v in that lens's frame (h positive toward its axis - 90 deg, v up).
